# Cache Individually, Not addAll

**Decision.** In the service worker's `install` handler, precache each URL with its own
`cache.add(url).catch(() => {})` inside a `Promise.all`, rather than the idiomatic
`cache.addAll(CORE)`.

**Date.** Present in `sw.js` at the first commit of [[physics-exam-prep]], 2026-07-10; file mtimes
put the code at 2026-06-30.

## Why

The reason is written on the line above the code:

> "      // addAll is atomic; cache individually so one miss doesn't abort install"
> — Physics/exam_prep/sw.js, 2026-07-10

`addAll` is specified to reject if **any** request fails, and a rejected `install` means the worker
never activates — so the app has no offline cache at all. With a `CORE` list of 33 entries (app
shell, five scripts, stylesheet, manifest, icon, three KaTeX files and 20 fonts), a single renamed
or mistyped path takes the entire offline capability down, and it does so silently at the one moment
the user is offline.

## The trade being made

| | `addAll` | per-URL `add().catch()` |
|---|---|---|
| One asset missing | install fails, **no** offline cache | install succeeds, cache is **quietly incomplete** |
| Failure visible | immediately, loudly | never, at runtime |
| Recovery | fix the path, redeploy | the `fetch` handler falls through to network — which is unavailable offline |

This is not strictly the safer option; it is the option that **fails partially instead of totally**,
and it converts a loud failure into a silent one. It is only defensible with something that catches
the missing file before shipping — and that thing exists.

## What makes it safe

`tools/qa.mjs` check 8, "Service worker precache vs index.html", is the compensating control. It
fails if any local asset `index.html` loads is absent from `sw.js`'s `CORE` array, and separately if
any concrete `CORE` path does not exist on disk. So the class of bug that `addAll`'s atomicity would
have caught at runtime is caught statically instead, before the code ships — and by a harness that
needs no browser. See [[generated-audit-artifact]] for the same instinct applied to the question
banks.

The README records that this check was not theoretical:

> "caught a real offline bug (the service worker wasn't caching the newly added scripts; fixed and"
> — Physics/exam_prep/README.md, 2026-07-10

## Alternatives rejected

| Option | Why not |
|---|---|
| **`cache.addAll(CORE)`** | the incumbent idiom; one bad path kills the whole install |
| **Precache nothing, cache on first fetch** | first offline visit renders nothing; defeats [[offline-first-static-deliverable]] |
| **Split into a required core and an optional tail** | more code and a policy decision per asset; not taken |
